flagged.evidence: The paragraph asserts existence of a nonremovable zero-area Jordan curve, but Facts F1–F6 and Proof 1.1–3.1 establish the disk witness and positive-area examples only; no local proof or proved item dependency supplies this comparison. Its only support is an external source citation. The repository’s SCHEMA.md says citations document sources and do not replace local proofs.

The wording assigns one curve Γ zero Λ_h measure for every gauge h(t)=o(t). Bishop’s Theorem 2 states “for any Hausdorff measure function h such that h(t)=o(t) ... there is a flexible curve Γ such that Λ_h(Γ)=0,” which gives a curve for each prescribed gauge, not one curve for all gauges. [Bishop, Theorem 2, p. 324](https://www.acadsci.fi/mathematica/Vol19/bishop.pdf).

The inversion formula has the wrong conjugate. For α=1, β=0, γ=−4 and p=3i, the original circle is |z|=2 and z=2 maps to w=(2+3i)/13. Substitution of z=p+1/w gives the coefficient αp+β̄=3i, whereas the proof uses αp̄+β̄=−3i; its displayed equation does not contain that image point. The conclusion that the transformed set is a circle remains recoverable with the corrected coefficient.
